title: Book One · Chapter 12: A Sheet of Paper
story:
On Friday afternoon, Leo comes to the green gate with his mother.

She looks at the school note and speaks to Mum. She will come back before dinner. Leo has to stay inside the yard.

"I know," Leo says.

"I still need to tell you," his mother says.

The boys put their things on the table. The bamboo strips are on the table too. Dad put them there. The ends feel smooth. Mum gives them a small pot of paste and a brush.

"That's enough for today," she says. "Keep it off the bedding."

Leo holds the brown bag open. Ronan cuts down one side. It opens into a long sheet.

They both look pleased. Then it rolls up again.

"Stay," Leo tells it.

It rolls up again. They put books on the corners. Ronan uses his red-sail book on one end. Leo puts a school book at the other.

The bag has old folds and a dark mark near the bottom. Ronan turns it over. The mark is still there.

"It goes through," he says.

"We can make that the back."

They lay the strips in a cross. One is longer than the other. Leo puts the short strip very near the top.

Ronan moves it lower. Leo moves it back.

"Look at the picture," Ronan says.

The picture shows the kite from one side. Part of one stick is hidden. Where do the two sticks meet? They cannot see.

Ronan draws around the cross. His first line is far from the wood. The next line is close. He joins the lines. One side is round near the top.

Leo laughs.

"It looks like a fat fish."

"You do it."

Leo takes the pencil. His line makes a sharp corner. The two sides do not match.

Mum comes to take the cups away. She looks at the shape.

"Do you want the two sides to match?"

"Yes," both boys say.

"How can you check?"

Ronan picks up one corner. The paper folds along the long middle stick. The two lines do not meet.

He takes the sticks off. He folds the sheet down the middle and presses the fold flat.

"Draw on this side," he tells Leo. "Then we can cut both at once."

The paper is thick at one old fold. Their scissors stop. Mum makes two small cuts there. The boys watch her hands. She gives the scissors back.

At last they open the sheet. Two sides spread out together. The dark mark is still there, but the shape is much better.

"We made a fish with two good sides," Leo says.

They paste the edges around the strips. Leo uses too much paste at first. It runs onto his thumb.

"Don't move," Ronan says. "We can put you in the class display."

Leo's mother comes back. The kite lies on a board. The paste is still wet. The boys cannot lift it yet.

Leo looks unhappy about leaving it. Ronan writes LEO beside his own name on the board's paper cover.

"It'll still be half yours tomorrow," he says.

Leo touches one dry corner with a finger. Then he puts the string beside the board. They will fly the kite another day. They will need the string then.
studyGuide:
## 先看情节提示也可以

两人开始剪纸做风筝，发现先对折再剪能让两边相同；做好的纸还要晾干。

## 从认词到读句子

1. **Mum / gives them / a small pot of paste and a brush.** 妈妈／给他们／一小罐浆糊和一把刷子；them指两个男孩。
2. **The boys / cannot lift it / yet.** 两个男孩／还不能拿起它／此时；it指还没干的风筝。

---

重点表达：flat＝平的；paste＝浆糊；match＝相配、对应；folds＝折痕；fold也表示折叠。

理解问题：

1. 纸摊开后出现了什么问题？
2. Ronan 从第一次剪纸中发现了什么？
